items.reason: The document explicitly lists testing business logic in contracts as an anti-pattern and tells readers to keep contracts thin.
All consumer test response bodies use Matchers (integer, string, regex, eachLike) and the document instructs using them so contracts assert types, not brittle values.
The compose file injects DB_PASSWORD and PACT_BROKER_PASSWORD from the environment and the document warns that hardcoding them leaks secrets.
The document repeatedly states never to skip can-i-deploy on main and gates both pipelines on it.

items.text: one massive pact covering every endpoint
items.reason: Listed as an anti-pattern; the document recommends starting with critical integration points and adding incrementally.

items.text: business logic validation in contract test
items.reason: Consumer test assertions only check shape (id, name defined, email contains @) and the document says business rules belong in unit/integration tests.
Provider stateHandlers seed or delete users in a real test database and skipping provider states is called out as an anti-pattern.

items.text: hardcoded values instead of parameterized states
items.reason: The document models parameterized states (given("user exists", { id: 123 })) and explicitly contrasts them with value-baked state names as the worse option.
The validateAgainstSpec helper throws on missing operation, missing schema, and on validation failure with validate.errors included.
Response data in the consumer tests is wrapped in matchers throughout; no raw hardcoded response bodies are modeled.

items.text: not using eachLike for array responses
items.reason: The paginated list example uses eachLike for the data array.
